{

  "type": "module",
  "description": "Dropbox AgentFS API examples running in Vercel Sandbox",
  "engines": { "node": ">=24.0.0" },
  "files": ["README.md", ".env.example", "src/", "scripts/", "test/", "reports/"],
  "scripts": {
    "demo": "node --env-file-if-exists=.env src/demo.mjs --agents 1",
    "demo:multi": "node --env-file-if-exists=.env src/demo.mjs --agents 3",
    "test": "node --test test/*.test.mjs",

    "check:package": "node scripts/check-package.mjs"
  },
  "dependencies": { "sandbox": "4.5.0" }
}

# Dropbox AgentFS + Vercel Sandbox

Run Dropbox AgentFS file operations from isolated Vercel Sandboxes. This example creates a new Dropbox folder, grants an agent access to that folder, and passes its short-lived token to a sandbox that writes and reads a sample file.

The optional three-agent demo starts three sandboxes with separate agent identities. It tests simultaneous writes to separate files and competing revision-checked updates to the same file.

This is an API example for partner evaluation. It does not mount Dropbox as a local filesystem, run an LLM, or implement production OAuth or token renewal. AgentFS access must be enabled for your Dropbox app. Confirm public sharing with Dropbox before publishing material based on its preview APIs.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or later and npm on your trusted host. Workers use the Node 24 Sandbox image.
- A Vercel account and project with Sandbox access. Running the examples consumes Sandbox usage.
- A Dropbox app enabled for AgentFS, with the AgentFS management permissions described in [application setup](https://docs.dropboxapi.com/agentfs/docs/get-started/application-setup).
- A user access token for that app with `files.metadata.read`, `files.content.read`, `files.content.write`, and the AgentFS management scope(s) granted during onboarding. Adding app permissions may require generating a fresh token.

## Setup

Clone the example and install its dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vercel-labs/vercel-dropbox-agentfs.git
cd vercel-dropbox-agentfs
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx --no-install sandbox login
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
```

Edit `.env` locally. Set `DROPBOX_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`, and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` to your own values. Keep the `.env` file private and do not paste its contents into logs or issues. Find the Vercel team and project IDs in their dashboard settings. The examples require explicit IDs and do not select a default project.

For a test with your own Dropbox account, generate a user access token in your enabled app's OAuth 2 settings. Dropbox's [quickstart](https://docs.dropboxapi.com/agentfs/docs/get-started/quickstart) describes this flow. Connecting other users requires an OAuth implementation outside this example.

The pinned `sandbox` CLI is installed by `npm ci`. The commands use its saved local login; a global CLI install is not required. Do not put the Dropbox app secret or documentation password in this project.

## Run one agent

```bash
npm run demo
```

The trusted host checks access, creates a unique folder and agent, and mints a restricted token. One sandbox uploads `A.txt`, downloads it, and checks the exact contents. The host preserves the result and stops the sandbox.

## Run three agents simultaneously

```bash
npm run demo:multi
```

Three agents get read/write access to the same new test folder, each with its own token and sandbox. They write `A.txt`, `B.txt`, and `C.txt` at a scheduled start time, then each reads all three files.

The test also creates three shared files. In each round, all three agents try to update one shared file using the same starting revision and different contents. It expects one `200` and two `409 path/conflict/file/` responses, then verifies that all agents read the winning contents and revision. The `409` responses in these rounds are expected conflicts, not setup failures.

The test requires three-way overlap in the recorded client request intervals. This timing check assumes the sandbox clocks are synchronized; it does not measure Dropbox's internal processing order. A missed start time or lack of overlap fails the run rather than being reported as simultaneous execution.

Revision checks prevent the rejected updates in these tests from silently replacing the winner. Applications still need to handle a conflict by rereading the file and deciding what to do next. This example does not merge changes or retry writes automatically. Unconditional overwrite behavior is not tested.

## Results and cleanup

Successful runs print `"result":"PASSED"` and a private `results/<run-id>/run.json` path. The summary includes verified file counts, race outcomes, and client request overlap. HTTP and CLI receipts include timestamps and request IDs for troubleshooting.

`results/` is ignored by Git and excluded from the package. It contains private account/resource identifiers and temporary `.runtime-*.json` credentials, so do not share the directory. Runtime tokens expire according to Dropbox's returned `expires_in`; they are not refreshed or automatically revoked by this demo. Do not commit `.env` or runtime files.

Each sandbox has a five-minute timeout, one vCPU, no exposed ports, no persistent snapshot, and outbound access restricted to Dropbox API domains. Names include a full random UUID. The host retrieves receipts before stopping sandboxes whose creation succeeded, including after later failures. It never stops a sandbox based only on an attempted creation. If creation times out with an unknown outcome, inspect the recorded name; any session created by that request has the five-minute timeout. If a stop request fails, the command exits nonzero and retains the name for inspection.

Dropbox test folders and agents are deliberately retained, as are Sandbox entities and local receipts. Review those resources in the respective dashboards before removing anything. This example never deletes existing user files or automatically deletes failed-run evidence.

The user token stays on the trusted host. It is excluded from the CLI subprocess environment. Each VM receives only its own agent token, not your user token or other agents' credentials.

## Troubleshooting

- `401` or expired token: obtain a fresh Dropbox user token, update `.env`, and run again. Each run uses a new folder; writes are not retried automatically.
- Missing AgentFS permissions or preview access: check app onboarding and permissions with Dropbox. Successful ordinary Dropbox API calls alone do not establish AgentFS access.
- Vercel auth or project errors: run `npx --no-install sandbox login` and check the explicit team/project IDs.
- Unexpected `409`, `500`, or worker failure: preserve the private receipts and request IDs. Share a redacted extract rather than credentials or the entire results directory.
- Interrupted host process: inspect recorded sandbox names; the five-minute timeout still applies. Automatic receipt collection is not guaranteed after force-killing the host.

## Checks

These commands run locally without creating Dropbox or Sandbox resources:

```bash
npm test
npm run check
npm run check:package
```

The examples use native HTTP requests matching Dropbox's documented API shapes. Dropbox also documents generating TypeScript or Python clients from its OpenAPI schema; this example does not redistribute that schema or its protected documentation. No upstream repository is required to run this code.

See [validation results](reports/validation.md) for tested behavior and limitations. Reference docs: [Dropbox authentication](https://docs.dropboxapi.com/agentfs/docs/concepts/authentication), [Dropbox workspaces](https://docs.dropboxapi.com/agentfs/docs/concepts/workspaces), and [Sandbox CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/cli-reference). Dropbox documentation may require preview access.

# Validation

The API prototype passed single-agent file roundtrips and two- and three-agent concurrency tests on October 9, 2026. The three-agent prototype used separate Vercel Sandboxes and scoped tokens. All three separate-file uploads succeeded, every agent read every output, and each of three same-file races returned one successful update and two revision conflicts. Final contents and revisions matched the winner. All sandboxes were stopped.

The packaged example also passed from a clean local copy on October 9, 2026, using Node 26.10.0 on the trusted host, the pinned Sandbox CLI 4.5.0, and Node 24.19.0 in the Sandboxes. Installation from the lockfile, offline tests, syntax/setup checks and the package-content scan passed. The local suite now contains 20 tests, including regression checks for CLI deadlines, confirmed resource ownership, rejecting non-file conflict errors, and source paths containing spaces.

| Packaged command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run demo` | One upload and exact-byte download passed; one Sandbox stopped. |
| `npm run demo:multi` | Three uploads and nine exact-byte cross-reads passed; all three Sandboxes stopped. |
| Same-file round 1 | One 200, two path/conflict/file/ 409 responses; 1,160 ms three-way client overlap. |
| Same-file round 2 | One 200, two path/conflict/file/ 409 responses; 1,171 ms three-way client overlap. |
| Same-file round 3 | One 200, two path/conflict/file/ 409 responses; 1,235 ms three-way client overlap. |

The table records the clean-copy rerun after the review fixes, from a checkout whose path contains spaces. The three separate-file writes overlapped for 1,196 ms. Overlap is derived as the earliest response completion minus the latest request start. All agents read the winning content and revision after each race. Private request IDs, source hashes and logs are retained outside this report. A fresh-login flow was not exercised; the clean copy used the host's existing Sandbox CLI login.

Scope: small text files, deterministic API workers and revision-checked updates. No LLM-driven assistants, mount/FUSE, automatic merge or retry, token renewal, production OAuth, permission-isolation audit, load test or unconditional-overwrite test. Client interval overlap assumes synchronized VM clocks; server-internal timing was not observed.

No credentials, private app/team/project IDs, sandbox IDs or raw partner logs are included in this report. This is an example for partner review.
